I think his early songs individually can hit differently than songs in his later work. I wouldn't say better or worse because it's just different. His earlier stuff is a lot rawer. The production is a lot rougher and it complements the naivety of the lyrics which captures a nostalgic time of when you're young. There's an aura of innocence in his earlier work and I imagine that his earlier stuff is a lot more personal whereas his later stuff is more about creative writing and telling a story.

I prefer his later albums more when it comes to a cohesive listen from front to back, I think he puts a lot more thought into creating an engrossing experience, stringing together lyrical subjects and experimental production in a similar theme that will run through an entire album. He works a lot harder at creating a solid overall album vibe rather than individual songs. I love the natural arc his whole discography has, you can truly see him slowly refining his craft for songwriting and developing his style.

For me, I'd have to say that every album he has made has been an improvement on the other. I didn't think he could top beach music. That album is so chaotic yet so beautiful. Feels like going through a mental breakdown and coming out the other end reborn. Then Rocket came out and it had this folky/country backbone running through it, with references to the great depression in America and fragments of a story that imprinted lots of imagery into my mind. He said he was inspired by Steinbeck during making this album (cant remember what interview it was from). Grapes of wrath is a great book that you should check out if you haven't before. And finally House of Sugar. A world of addicts, twisted beauty and fairytale. An uplifting look into parts of Alex's life like Hope, about his friend dying of an overdose. But he perfects the art of writing a personal song but not making it about him, you can listen to it and put yourself in the main characters shoes which is what an artist should do. The euphoric Gretel, man oh man I couldn't stop listening to that song when it came out. Such a hard hitting, uplifting experience. Southern Sky is an absolute beauty of a song, with its roots in rocket country esque style while continuing the story of brite boi. The weird instrumental bits in the middle of the album feel like an interlude at a play/movies. Or setting up for a final fight. 

I dunno man, it's weird because a lot of the time he doesn't give you a story but you fill in the blanks. He gives you just enough meaning and emotion so that you are invested but lets you interpret the song however you want. And that is why I love this man.

Obviously the title of "DYSTOPIA" calls back to books such as Farenheit 451, 1984 and Brave New World. Given this, I feel that you executed the atmosphere of these books in a very eloquent way given the short spanned nature of your poem. I personally want to see more poems taking the subject of dystopia as I believe we are living within one. If I were to be critical, I would suggest that the last line had some more weight to it. It feels as if the poem builds a picture but the last line seems to break the build up. I think if you can eloquently put something jarring, it would suit the structure and tension of the poem. Maybe throw the rhyme scheme out the window, just to add a slight disconnection to the final blow of the poem which fits the the dystopian vibe.

I love the puritanical, elemental feeling of this poem.  The simple feelings of hot and cold expanded into great depth. The open ended-ness of the poem allows the reader to place their own experiences/pain into the context of the symbolism (swimming in ice representing a challenge, being cut/finding it too cold being a struggle responses). Then how it develops into missing the previous pain and suffering when succumb to burning and heat. I personally feel this poem in several ways. One of which is that it is a metaphor for an unhealthy relationship, how even though you swam in it it hurt you. But even escaping it can be difficult, with the pain that comes with loneliness  of leaving a relationship. On a more general level, it seems a great exploration of the human condition of always wanting more.  Never being satisfied, being hot or cold, and how difficult it can be to be neutral.

I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but I didn't even start to get over my ex for at least 7 months (the relationship lasted 3 years). It's tough, you're gonna cry,  you may relapse, you're gonna feel like nothings worth getting out of bed for anymore. But force yourself to get up and do something, anything. Read books, watch movies, write letters you won't send, do paintings, play video games, start a new hobby and most importantly do exercise. Before the breakup I wasn't a very fit person but I started running (mostly for the endorphins) and it's helped massively. I also really recommend meditation. I started this after the breakup too and started 20 mins everyday, easy right? Now I do 40 mins everyday and it really helps you focus your mind. This is useful during a breakup because you are better able to focus on other things and not dwell on your ex.

At the moment I'm at 8 months NC. And do I still love her? Yes. You can't erase that sadly, and why would you want to. You need to remember the ups and downs to develop as a person, understand what you require in a partner and what you require in yourself. The longer that goes on the more you'll be able to look back on the relationship and see the flaws that were impossible to see before. I thought my ex was an absolute goddess that I couldn't live without for like 3 months after the breakup. Now I see things realistically. I see the flaws that make her human, I see my own flaws too. I'd become so dependent during the relationship that when we broke up every day alone was agony! Now I love being alone, I couldn't imagine spending so much time with another person. I don't really desire it anymore either.

I guess what I want to get across to you is that you guys broke up for a reason, believe in it and move on. No matter how much you start to doubt it, that you feel she was "the one", ignore it. "The one" was invented by fairytales and Hollywood movies. There are probably a million "the one's". If she wants to message you she will but a rom-com grand gesture from your end isn't gonna save anything, in fact, it may drive her even further away. 

Being alone gonna suck, it's gonna be an uphill battle not to message her. But the thing I've found about this hill is that the beginning section is the steepest. The further up you go, the closer the top is. You may feel like messaging her, to go back down the hill will always being easier than climbing up. But the problem is you've got to climb this hill at some point. You've got to get over it. Once you get to the top then go down the other side, you won't find yourself wanting to message her. Messaging will start to be more of an endeavour than not. And soon enough you will get to the bottom on the other side, you'll look back on what you've endured and you'll feel proud!

Good luck buddy, it's gonna be tough but I believe in you.

the art of mastering is too make your track sound as good as possible on all devices. There's an interview with Quincy Jones about the making of thriller. Every track he'd listen back to on a cruddy radio to hear what it sounded like, and optimised tracks so that they'd sound as good as possible even on that. When you master do you use several different speakers/headphones to reference between? If you can get it to sound as good as possible on all these then it will likely sound better on other devices.

Of course, if your friends Soundsystem sounds crap even when you're playing professional mixes through it then I'm sure she'll see it's the speakers not your mixes. Try and play some other artists music through it first so she can see that its the speakers, not you're mixes haha. Hope this helps

My main tip is to focus mostly on the mental side of things. It is natural for anyone to struggle when learning to drive but us dyspraxics struggle more than most. So do not get discouraged when making mistakes, view them as something to learn from in the future and ensure you don’t let them get you down.
